title: Perplexity robots.txt Compliance Policy
excerpt: Perplexity respects robots.txt directives. Our crawler, PerplexityBot, will not index the full or partial text content of any site that disallows it via robots.txt. However, if a page is blocked, we may still index the domain, headline, and a brief factual summary. Perplexity partners with third-party crawlers to help build our search index and has updated its agreements to ensure these providers also respect robots.txt, particularly for news publisher sites.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-29 (session_10, GB-001): the original URL (perplexity.ai/hub/faq/robots-txt-compliance) 404s; live URL is the Perplexity Help Center article above, confirmed 200 on 2026-08-29. This help-center article does not itself state the Perplexity-User exemption; that half of the original excerpt is independently confirmed instead by SRC-059 (EV-123).

title: We Tracked 1,885 Pages Adding Schema. AI Citations Barely Moved.
excerpt: "Adding schema produced no major uplift in citations on any platform." Table: Google AIO -4.6% ("Small but statistically significant decline relative to matched controls"); Google AI Mode +2.4% ("Statistically indistinguishable from zero"); ChatGPT +2.2% ("Statistically indistinguishable from zero"). "AI Overview citations on treated pages fell by 4.6% relative to control pages, and the result is 'statistically significant' (the odds of seeing a gap this large by pure chance are about 1 in 2,500)." Every page in the dataset had 100+ AI Overview citations before treatment, so the study speaks to pages already inside AI's consideration set, not cold/uncited pages.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-08-29 (session_10, GB-002): correct slug is /schema-ai-citations/ (not /schema-markup-ai-search/ or /ai-search-schema-study/), confirmed 200 on 2026-08-29. Title "We Tracked 1,885 Pages Adding Schema. AI Citations Barely Moved." confirmed verbatim, published 2026-05-11, authors Louise Linehan and Xibeijia Guan confirmed. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the AI Overviews -4.6% figure is explicitly reported by Ahrefs as statistically significant (p ~ 1/2500), NOT within noise as KT-007's prior statement/uncertainty text implied — only the AI Mode +2.4% and ChatGPT +2.2% figures are noise. title: The rise of the AI crawler
excerpt: The data indicates that while ChatGPT and Claude crawlers do fetch JavaScript files (ChatGPT: 11.50%, Claude: 23.84% of requests), they don't execute them. They can't read client-side rendered content.
notes: Independent server-log study by Vercel and MERJ across top web properties measuring AI crawler request behavior and JavaScript execution.

title: Overview of OpenAI Crawlers
excerpt: OpenAI uses OAI-SearchBot and GPTBot robots.txt tags to enable webmasters to manage how their sites and content work with AI. Each setting is independent of the others.

title: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web, and how can site owners block the crawler?
excerpt: ClaudeBot helps enhance the utility and safety of our generative AI models by collecting web content that could include training data... Anthropic's Bots respect 'do not crawl' signals by honoring industry standard directives in robots.txt.
notes: Official Anthropic guidance specifying ClaudeBot crawler function and webmaster controls via robots.txt.

title: Fix canonicalization issues
excerpt: The canonical link element is not recommended for those who want to avoid duplication by syndication partners, because the pages are often very different. The most effective solution is for partners to block indexing of your content.
notes: Google Search Central troubleshooting guidance confirming rel=canonical is not recommended for syndication and advising noindex/blocking instead.

title: Google's neural matching versus RankBrain: How Google uses each in search
excerpt: Neural matching is an AI-based system Google began using in 2018 primarily to understand how words are related to concepts... it helps better relate words to searches... even if the exact words aren't used.
notes: Search Engine Land reporting on Google Search Liaison confirmation of neural matching deployment in 2018.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
excerpt: We introduce RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever.
notes: Foundational research paper defining Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al., NeurIPS 2020).

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
excerpt: In this work, we show that retrieval can be practically implemented using dense representations alone, where embeddings are learned from a small number of questions and passages by a simple dual-encoder framework. When evaluated on a wide range of open-domain QA datasets, our dense retriever outperforms a strong Lucene-BM25 system largely by 9%-19% absolute.
notes: Academic research establishing dense neural passage retrieval outperforming traditional BM25/TF-IDF sparse vector search.
